questions.q: Find $\int 2x(x^2+1)^4\,dx$ using the substitution $u=x^2+1$.
Find $\int x\sqrt{x^2+9}\,dx$ using the substitution $u=x^2+9$.

Find $\int 3x^2(x^3-2)^4\,dx$ using the substitution $u=x^3-2$.
Find $\int xe^x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
Find $\int x\cos x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=x$, $dv=\cos x\,dx$, so $du=dx$, $v=\sin x$. $\int x\cos x\,dx=x\sin x-\int\sin x\,dx=x\sin x+\cos x+C$.

questions.q: Find $\int\ln x\,dx$ using integration by parts with $u=\ln x$ and $dv=dx$.
Find $\int x^2e^x\,dx$ using integration by parts twice.
questions.answer: Let $u=x^2$, $dv=e^x\,dx$: $\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-\int2xe^x\,dx$. From an earlier result, $\int xe^x\,dx=e^x(x-1)+C$, so $\int2xe^x\,dx=2e^x(x-1)+C$. Result: $x^2e^x-2e^x(x-1)+C=e^x(x^2-2x+2)+C$.

sections.heading: Integrating trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions

questions.q: Find $\int\sin(3x)\,dx$ and $\int e^{2x}\,dx$.
Find $\int\dfrac{4x}{x^2+1}\,dx$.
Find $\int\tan x\,dx$, using the substitution $u=\cos x$.
questions.answer: $\tan x=\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$. With $u=\cos x$, $du=-\sin x\,dx$: $\int\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\,dx=-\int\dfrac{du}{u}=-\ln|u|+C=-\ln|\cos x|+C=\ln|\sec x|+C$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: designing a vase

questions.q: This question has three parts. A vase is formed by rotating the curve $y=\sqrt{x}$, for $0\leq x\leq9$ (cm), about the $y$-axis, where $x$ is horizontal distance from the axis and $y$ is height. (a) Express $x^2$ in terms of $y$, and evaluate $V=\pi\int_0^3x^2\,dy$ to find the volume of the vase. (b) A cylindrical base of radius $3$ cm and height $2$ cm is attached underneath. Find the total volume, to two decimal places (using $\pi\approx3.14159$). (c) Show that the volume of water filled to height $h$ (ignoring the base) is $V(h)=\dfrac{\pi h^5}{5}$, and find the height $h$ at which the water volume equals half the vase's volume from part (a), to two decimal places.
questions.answer: (a) Since $y=\sqrt{x}$, $x=y^2$, so $x^2=y^4$, and $y$ ranges from $0$ to $3$ (as $x=9\Rightarrow y=3$). $V=\pi\int_0^3y^4\,dy=\pi\left[\dfrac{y^5}{5}\right]_0^3=\dfrac{243\pi}{5}=48.6\pi$. (b) Cylinder volume: $\pi(3)^2(2)=18\pi$. Total: $48.6\pi+18\pi=66.6\pi\approx66.6(3.14159)\approx209.23$ cm$^3$. (c) $V(h)=\pi\int_0^hy^4\,dy=\dfrac{\pi h^5}{5}$. Setting this equal to half of $48.6\pi$, i.e. $24.3\pi$: $\dfrac{h^5}{5}=24.3\Rightarrow h^5=121.5\Rightarrow h=121.5^{1/5}\approx2.61$ cm.
